routines.semantics: raw.vaddg(a,b) returns every component of actual CSPICE a+b in a new owned array. Order, finite-input overflow and signed numerical results are retained; empty inputs return an empty array after the canonical call. Inputs are readonly dense finite-number arrays, the dimension is inferred from length, paired vectors must have equal lengths, and results do not alias input/heap storage. Dimension must fit signed32. WASM additionally retains the existing 256 MiB per-vector-buffer cap.

scenarios.observes: Observe an actual canonical empty-only C call with guarded non-null storage and no vector writes; empty output shape reaches comparison.
Observe positive/negative/zero or mixed singleton inputs through actual vaddg, distinguishing dimension one from a fixed three-component path.
Observe complete array output at dimensions 2,4,7 with signed entries beyond the third position. Swapped input observations retain the routine's actual symmetry or ordered result.
Observe either zero operand, parallel/opposed and orthogonal axes; compare every component of the sums.
Observe both 1e100 and 1e-100 input scales through actual vaddg. Focused live rescaling makes each tiny output component or scalar observable.

routines.edgeAssessment: Signed mixed dimensions, reversed operands, both zero positions, axes and wide scales exercise every sum entry; finite-input extremes additionally retain overflow. Tagged live extremes compare every component of [Inf,-Inf,0,3], plus a finite MAX/4 control.
routines.errorAssessment: NAIF/pinned source provides no ordinary scientific error for these defined finite vectors. Registered cases observe actual successful values, including empty dimension. Malformed/nonfinite arrays, unequal dimensions, invalid coefficients and unsafe dimensions/byte counts are explicit wrapper-safety tests; no invented SPICE error or execution of undefined giant dimensions is claimed.
routines.fixtureRationale: Project-authored numeric vectors only; no external dataset or kernel fixture. Empty-oracle guards and allocation-failure instrumentation are test infrastructure, not scientific data substitutions.
routines.cleanup: Kernel-free authored numeric inputs require no files, handles, kernels or retained scientific resources. Shared C validates dimension/non-null buffers and invokes the actual routine; adapters return results only after status checking. Errors collect diagnostics/reset before throwing. Native vectors reserve valid sentinel storage at dimension zero, and all outputs are copied into owned arrays/objects. WASM uses checked byte lengths, transactional withAllocs, valid non-null empty sentinels and copied results before release. Allocation fault/success checks and ownership tests are separate from live scientific value comparisons.
routines.tolerance: Normal numeric comparison remains atol=1e-12/rtol=1e-12 across every scalar/vector component; booleans and output shapes are exact. Focused scaled live checks strengthen tiny outputs without global tolerance changes. Focused tagged live comparison retains complete array/object shape, compares NaN/Inf/zero signs exactly and finite nonzero values with relative-only 1e-12 tolerance; no global comparator change.

routines.semantics: raw.unormg(v) returns a fresh {unit,norm}, with every unit component in an owned array and the actual separate norm output. Zero input returns a zero unit array/norm zero; empty input returns {unit:[],norm:0}. Computed norm overflow/underflow effects are preserved; the adapter does not independently derive or correct either output. Inputs are readonly dense finite-number arrays, the dimension is inferred from length, paired vectors must have equal lengths, and results do not alias input/heap storage. The safe dimension ceiling is 2147483646 because pinned f2c one-based loops would overflow at INT32_MAX. WASM additionally retains the existing 256 MiB per-vector-buffer cap.

scenarios.observes: Observe an actual canonical empty-only C call with guarded non-null storage and no vector writes; both empty unit array and returned norm zero reach comparison.
Observe positive/negative/zero or mixed singleton inputs through actual unormg, distinguishing dimension one from a fixed three-component path.
Observe complete unit array and norm at dimensions 2,4,7 with signed entries beyond the third position.
Observe a four-component zero vector and a seven-component vector with only its final entry nonzero; both unit and norm must reflect the tail.
Observe both 1e100 and 1e-100 input scales through actual unormg. Both unit and norm are compared, with only norm rescaled in focused tests.

routines.edgeAssessment: Both output fields are observed for empty/zero, signed singleton, full multi-dimensional and tail-only inputs. Scale changes preserve ordinary unit direction while changing norm; numerical extremes retain actual outputs. Tagged live [MAX,-MAX,0,0] yields unit [0,-0,0,0] and norm Inf, with every field compared; a MAX/4 control is finite. Actual RPC preserves both the empty unit array and separate zero norm.
routines.errorAssessment: NAIF/pinned source provides no ordinary scientific error for these defined finite vectors. Registered cases observe actual successful values, including empty dimension. Malformed/nonfinite arrays, unequal dimensions, invalid coefficients and unsafe dimensions/byte counts are explicit wrapper-safety tests; no invented SPICE error or execution of undefined giant dimensions is claimed.
routines.fixtureRationale: Project-authored numeric vectors only; no external dataset or kernel fixture. Empty-oracle guards and allocation-failure instrumentation are test infrastructure, not scientific data substitutions.
routines.cleanup: Kernel-free authored numeric inputs require no files, handles, kernels or retained scientific resources. Shared C validates dimension/non-null buffers and invokes the actual routine; adapters return results only after status checking. Errors collect diagnostics/reset before throwing. Native vectors reserve valid sentinel storage at dimension zero, and all outputs are copied into owned arrays/objects. WASM uses checked byte lengths, transactional withAllocs, valid non-null empty sentinels and copied results before release. Allocation fault/success checks and ownership tests are separate from live scientific value comparisons.
routines.tolerance: Normal numeric comparison remains atol=1e-12/rtol=1e-12 across every scalar/vector component; booleans and output shapes are exact. Focused scaled live checks strengthen tiny outputs without global tolerance changes. Every unit entry and the distinct norm field reach comparison; norm scaling is independent of the unit array. Focused tagged live comparison retains complete array/object shape, compares NaN/Inf/zero signs exactly and finite nonzero values with relative-only 1e-12 tolerance; no global comparator change.

findings.summary: Locked SpiceyPy 6.0.3 calls unormg_c at dimension zero but its zero-length output converter raises IndexError afterward, so that wrapper cannot directly deliver the valid empty scientific result.
findings.repair: Use the independent general_vector_oracle empty-only typed binding to the exact locked library symbol with guarded non-null input/output storage and explicit dimension zero. Assert no vector storage writes; read the actual separate norm for unormg. Keep nonempty calls on SpiceyPy and compare registered empty outputs. No scientific algorithm, tspice substitute or new exclusion is introduced.

findings.summary: The typed adapters validated array entries and then read the caller-owned array again when delegating or marshaling. Those later values were not necessarily the ones validated.
findings.repair: Capture dimensions, enforce routine-specific count bounds and equal lengths where required, then copy each finite general-vector component once. Use the owned copies for dispatch, buffer sizes and output-length checks. Both native delegation and WASM marshaling use the validated snapshot. Bounded entry-read and ownership regressions check this adapter property independently of unchanged scientific cases.
